name: Belle II detector
notes: Overall dimensions other than the 8 m height quoted at the 2017 roll-in are not recorded: only the abstract page of the Belle II Technical Design Report (arXiv:1011.0352) was consulted, so no TDR geometry table is cited. Height: 'the entire 8 m-tall, 1400 tonne Belle II detector system' (belle2.jp, roll-in article); it is quoted here rather than recorded as a spec.
Per-subsystem quantities (channel counts, radii, crystal counts) are unresolved for the same reason.

placements.note: The roll-in placed the assembled detector at the SuperKEKB interaction point in the Tsukuba hall; it has been there since.
placements.quote: On 11 April, the Belle II detector was successfully “rolled-in” to the collision point [...] moving the entire 8 m-tall, 1400 tonne Belle II detector system from its assembly area to the beam-collision point 13 m away

solenoid_field.quote: a superconducting solenoid coil that provides a 1.5 Tesla magnetic field

total_mass.note: Mass of the complete detector system as moved at the 2017 roll-in.
total_mass.quote: moving the entire 8 m-tall, 1400 tonne Belle II detector system from its assembly area to the beam-collision point 13 m away

description.quote: two layers of pixelated silicon sensors (PXD) and four layers of double-sided silicon strip sensors (SVD)
description.value: Two layers of pixelated silicon sensors immediately around the beam pipe, measuring decay-vertex positions. A new, fully implemented pixel detector was installed during Long Shutdown 1.

description.quote: two layers of pixelated silicon sensors (PXD) and four layers of double-sided silicon strip sensors (SVD)
description.value: Four layers of double-sided silicon strip sensors surrounding the PXD.

description.quote: a central drift chamber (CDC) that measures trajectories, momenta and dE/dx information of charged particles
description.value: The main tracking device: a large gas volume strung with sense and field wires that measures charged-particle trajectories, momenta and specific ionisation (dE/dx).

description.quote: a barrel-shaped array of Time-Of-Propagation (TOP) counters
description.value: A barrel-shaped array of quartz-radiator Cherenkov counters used for charged-hadron identification.

description.quote: another ring-imaging Cherenkov counters with aerogel radiator in the forward end-cap (ARICH)
description.value: A ring-imaging Cherenkov counter with an aerogel radiator in the forward end-cap, complementing the TOP for particle identification.

description.quote: an electromagnetic calorimeter (ECL) comprised of scintillator crystals located inside a superconducting solenoid coil
description.value: Scintillator crystals inside the solenoid that measure the energies of photons and electrons.

description.quote: an iron flux-return located outside of the coil which is instrumented to detect K0L mesons and to identify muons (KLM)
description.value: The instrumented iron flux return outside the solenoid, which detects long-lived neutral kaons and identifies muons.

summary.plain: The detector that records what comes out of the SuperKEKB collisions. Seven layers of instruments, wrapped in a strong magnet, track and identify the particles produced when electrons and positrons annihilate.
summary.technical: General-purpose 4π spectrometer at the SuperKEKB interaction point: PXD, SVD, CDC, TOP and ARICH, ECL inside a 1.5 T solenoid, and the KLM in the instrumented flux return; about 1400 t, rolled in on 11 April 2017.

technology.quote: an electromagnetic calorimeter (ECL) comprised of scintillator crystals located inside a superconducting solenoid coil that provides a 1.5 Tesla magnetic field
technology.value: general-purpose 4π magnetic spectrometer with seven subdetectors inside a 1.5 T superconducting solenoid
